agent.problem: The blank asks for “servants,” but the opening card gives no context from which the baker could reason out that role rather than “prophets” or “elders.” The blank therefore tests wording the baker has not seen.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

agent.problem: This card retells both verse 4's praying with joy and verse 5's reason for that joy, but it cites only verse 5. Its citation should begin with the first verse it uses.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

agent.problem: Verse 6's “until the day of Christ Jesus” is never conveyed. Card 17's later mention of the day of Christ concerns being pure and blameless, not the completion of God's good work, so an important qualifier from verse 6 is missing.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

agent.problem: The question says “their growing love” and “helps them” without identifying whose love it is. The preceding story card is no longer visible, so the question needs to name the believers at Philippi.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

agent.problem: The walkthrough never positively states that the fruit of righteousness comes through Jesus Christ. Marking “their own hard work” false only rules out one possible source; it does not teach the actual source given in verse 11.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
